title: Canary-Controlled Safe-Data Interleaving for Reducing Emergent Misalignment

contributions.purpose: Mitigates emergent misalignment (EM) during fine-tuning by adjusting defense strength to the model's real-time risk state instead of using fixed interleaving ratios.
contributions.mechanism: A closed-loop canary-controlled adaptive interleaving framework that evaluates canary prompts during training, computes an EMA-smoothed risk estimate, and adjusts the safe-data interleaving ratio via a threshold-based policy with hysteresis.
contributions.evaluation: On the Security EM benchmark with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, achieves 5.39% General %Misaligned vs 7.15% for fixed 5% interleaving (25% relative improvement).
contributions.source_quote: We introduce a canary-controlled adaptive interleaving framework that monitors EM risk during fine-tuning and dynamically adjusts the safe-data interleaving ratio based on real-time behavioral signals.

contributions.purpose: Establishes that adaptive interleaving outperforms fixed-ratio safe-data interleaving in both mean misalignment and stability.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of the canary-controlled method against a fixed 5% interleaving baseline across multiple seeds on the Security EM benchmark.
contributions.evaluation: 5.39% General %Misaligned vs 7.15% for fixed 5% interleaving, a 25% relative improvement, with 4x lower cross-seed variance.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate empirically that our method achieves 5.39% General %Misaligned compared to 7.15% for fixed 5% interleaving—a 25% relative improvement—with 4x lower cross-seed variance on the Security EM benchmark.

contributions.purpose: Isolates the source of the improvement, showing adaptive timing itself matters beyond the average amount of safe data used.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies comparing adaptive timing against fixed-timing variants with identical safe-data volume, and removing EMA smoothing and hysteresis from the controller.
contributions.evaluation: Fixed-timing variants show 36% worse performance despite identical safe-data volume; EMA smoothing and hysteresis are shown to be critical for stable controller behavior.
contributions.source_quote: We conduct ablation studies showing that adaptive timing provides value beyond average interleaving ratio (36% degradation with fixed timing), and that EMA smoothing and hysteresis are critical for stable controller behavior.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work draws inspiration from adaptive methods in machine learning that dynamically adjust training parameters based on feedback signals.

However, existing approaches to safe-data interleaving use fixed ratios throughout training (Kaczér et al., 2025), potentially applying insufficient intervention when EM risk is high or unnecessary intervention when risk is low. Our canary-controlled approach addresses this limitation by using real-time risk estimation to adaptively adjust the interleaving ratio, bringing feedback control principles to safety-focused training.
